name: Singleton-Merten Dysplasia

criteria.description: Severe dental dysplasia including delayed tooth eruption and root hypoplasia
Early-onset calcification of the ascending aorta and cardiac valves
Clinical or laboratory evidence of type I interferonopathy
Osteopenia, widened medullary cavities, and acro-osteolysis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least three major criteria including dental anomalies, aortic calcification, and skeletal abnormalities, or genetic confirmation of IFIH1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for IFIH1 mutations is strongly recommended to confirm diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe dental dysplasia with delayed tooth eruption
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic dental root hypoplasia and abnormal tooth development

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early-onset calcification of ascending aorta and cardiac valves
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to valvular dysfunction and potential cardiac complications
searchTerms: early hardening of aorta and valves
calcification of heart vessels in young

pathognomonic.symptomName: Osteopenia with acro-osteolysis of distal phalanges
pathognomonic.notes: Bone resorption primarily affecting distal digits
searchTerms: low bone density with finger bone loss
bone thinning and finger tip bone damage

common.notes: May contribute to delayed motor milestones
Elevated intraocular pressure observed in some patients
Short stature and delayed growth patterns

occasional.symptomName: Dental caries due to enamel hypoplasia

rare.notes: Autoimmune involvement reported in isolated cases

laboratory: Elevated type I interferon signature in peripheral blood
imaging: Radiographic evidence of aortic and cardiac valve calcifications
Skeletal X-rays showing acro-osteolysis and widened medullary cavities
other: Dental radiographs showing root hypoplasia and delayed eruption

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of dental anomalies and aortic calcification
Lack of dental dysplasia and interferonopathy features
Diffuse skin thickening without vascular calcifications
No dental or skeletal abnormalities typical of Singleton-Merten dysplasia

redFlags: Early-onset aortic valve stenosis or insufficiency
Severe dental root hypoplasia with delayed eruption
Progressive acro-osteolysis leading to digital deformities
references: Singleton MV et al. Singleton-Merten syndrome: a rare interferonopathy with dental and skeletal abnormalities. Am J Med Genet A. 2011.
Rutsch F et al. Aortic and valvular calcifications, dental anomalies, and skeletal abnormalities in Singleton-Merten syndrome caused by mutations in IFIH1. Nat Genet. 2015.
Crow YJ et al. Type I interferonopathies: a novel set of inborn errors of immunity. J Clin Invest. 2015.
